overall.summary: The high heart rate gate is described as raising risk when it lowers it, and the ST depression gate is said to act more with a flat ST segment when the slope partner is a downsloping segment (which switches it off) and the amplifier is the thallium defect. All numbers reproduce.

findings.statement: This part raises the predicted risk for patients with a high maximum heart rate: ... then raises the risk steadily.
findings.check: probe --set cp=3 --sweep thalach=120:200:9; C54 direction; readout weight
findings.evidence: ann_34 contribution 0 up to 140 bpm, then -0.168 at 150, -0.715 at 160, -1.810 at 180, -2.905 at 200 (risk 2.7% -> 0.0%). C54 says 'lowers'; readout -0.918; the part's own evidence sentence says 'lowers'. The direction is reversed.
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-13f0ea --set cp=3 --sweep thalach=120:200:9

findings.statement: This part raises the predicted risk with ST depression on exercise, in an uneven way, and more so with a flat ST segment. [C37, C41]
findings.check: probe --sweep oldpeak=0:3:7 --sweep slope=1,2,3; C41 is the oldpeak x thal interaction
findings.evidence: the gate's contribution is identical for upsloping and flat segments (+0.215 at 1.5 mm, +1.427 at 3 mm in both) and 0 at every oldpeak with a downsloping segment. A flat segment does not change it; C41 (cited) is about a reversible thallium defect, which does amplify it (active 83% with thal 7 vs 27% without).
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-13f0ea --sweep oldpeak=0:3:7 --sweep slope=1,2,3

findings.evidence: all reproduce; 78 of 78 claims; prose numbers all found
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify recheck experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-13f0ea

findings.statement: AUC 0.947; linear core alone 0.930; mean-ablating each gate 0.938 / 0.940 / 0.945; core logit SD 4.90
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify ablate experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-13f0ea --part ann_32 --to mean
